title: Thermalization and quantum chaos in a pure gauge discrete non-Abelian lattice gauge theory
authors: Marco Vaia, Edoardo Ballini, Alberto Bottarelli, Matteo M. Wauters, Philipp Hauke
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26695v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gauge theories constitute the basis of our microscopic description of fundamental physical laws, and they are a cornerstone of contemporary scientific research. Yet, how such systems thermalize far from equilibrium remains a fundamental open question at the crossroads of statistical, high-energy, and condensed-matter physics. In this work, we investigate the thermalization properties of non-Abelian lattice gauge theories, focusing on the discrete gauge group $D_3$, which is ideally suited for current qudit-based quantum simulators. Specifically, we study a linear plaquette chain in a gauge-fixed formulation that removes unphysical degrees of freedom. A numerical analysis of the Hamiltonian spectrum and expectation values of local operators shows a behavior broadly aligned with the Eigenstate Thermalization Hypothesis (ETH). We also study thermalization through the real-time dynamics of the entanglement spectrum, confirming the emergence of random-matrix level statistics after an initial transient. Our results expand the rich phenomenology of dihedral non-Abelian gauge systems. Once the relevant symmetry structure is properly resolved, the model displays the same qualitative ETH-based thermalization scenario observed in Abelian gauge models and generic non-integrable quantum many-body systems.

title: Large deviations, effective dynamics, and dynamical phase transitions in random maps
authors: \'Angela Tajuelo-Valbuena, Jorge Hidalgo, Ricardo Guti\'errez, Carlos P\'erez-Espigares
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26704v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Large deviation theory provides a natural framework to characterize rare fluctuations of time-averaged observables in deterministic and stochastic systems. Building on previous results for deterministic chaotic maps, here we extend the Doob transform to random maps, constructing an effective dynamics in which rare events become typical. This makes it possible to directly reproduce the dynamics of rare trajectories that are exponentially difficult to sample under the original dynamics. We further apply spectral large-deviation methods to characterize dynamical phase transitions in random maps. The spectral structure of the tilted operator provides insight into the mechanisms underlying these transitions and, in particular, allows us to identify the appropriate initial states that select one dynamical phase or another. Our results extend the connection between large deviation theory, spectral methods, and effective dynamics to random chaotic maps, providing a general framework to study rare events and dynamical phase transitions in these systems.

title: Certification of non-stabilizerness in multi-qubit systems via worst-case random access codes
authors: Santiago Zamora
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26705v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recent works have proposed semi-device-independent frameworks to certify non-stabilizerness, but the complexity of the stabilizer polytope makes these methods infeasible beyond a few qubits. In this work, we address this limitation by moving to partially characterized measurements in the context of worst-case random access codes. We first establish a simple condition, which we term the stabilizer pigeonhole criterion, that certifies non-stabilizerness in $m$-qubit pure states, and show how it can be applied to reduced states. As an application, we certify magic in $W$ states of arbitrary size using only eight preparations and three single-qubit measurement settings. Motivated by recent work on the stabilizer marginal problem, we then construct prepare-and-measure correlations generated by global $m$-qubit quantum states for which every $k$-qubit marginal lies inside the stabilizer polytope, yet the combined correlations cannot be reproduced by any global stabilizer mixture. Finally, we derive analytical upper and lower bounds on the worst-case bias attainable with mixed stabilizer preparations in an $m$-qubit random access code with $n$ Pauli measurements. For the complete set of $4^m-1$ non-identity Pauli measurements, we show that the optimal quantum and mixed-stabilizer biases both scale as $2^{-3m/2}$, and that their ratio is asymptotically bounded by a constant ($\lesssim 1.85$), showing that in this setting, magic in the preparations alone yields at most a constant-factor advantage over stabilizer mixtures.

title: Improved Digitization Bounds for U(1) Lattice Gauge Theory via Semiclassical Analysis
authors: Di Fang, Yu Tong
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26720v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Simulating lattice gauge theories on a digital quantum computer or using tensor network methods requires a finite-dimensional approximation of the gauge field, a process often called digitization. Controlling the resulting error is essential for assessing the accuracy and resource requirements of these simulations. In this work, we derive a digitization error bound for low-lying eigenstates of the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian for pure U(1) gauge theory and translate it into a bound on time-evolution error. Compared with existing bounds, our result achieves exponentially improved dependence on the inverse lattice spacing $1/a$ and evolution time $T$, together with improved dependence on the inverse coupling $1/g$. The key idea is to identify a small parameter in the Kogut--Susskind Hamiltonian and apply tools from semiclassical analysis. Specifically, we adapt Agmon's method to establish exponential decay of the error with the truncation threshold. These results sharpen estimates of the local Hilbert space dimension and qubit resources needed to simulate gauge theories near the continuum limit, at weak coupling, and over long times.

title: Cavity-Controlled Hysteresis and Multilevel Molecular Switching in Hybrid Optomechanics
authors: Hugo Molinares, Ra\'ul Coto, Vitalie Eremeev, Eduardo Chamorro
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26724v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate cavity-controlled hysteresis and multilevel molecular switching in a hybrid molecular optomechanical system composed of a plasmonic nanocavity, a Fabry-P\'erot cavity, and an ensemble of molecular vibrations. Molecular-plasmonic optomechanical interaction together with cavity-plasmon hybridization produce bistability and dynamical hysteresis, leading to a history-dependent optical and molecular response. An analytical treatment of the steady-state equations shows that the auxiliary cavity renormalizes the effective optical linewidth and detuning, while the collective molecular interaction generates an effective nonlinearity. Together, these effects enable control of the hysteretic regime through optical detuning, cavity-plasmon coupling, and molecular ensemble size. Beyond bistability, pulsed excitation generates staircase-like molecular dynamics, with ascending or descending vibrational populations depending on the optical driving configuration. In particular, the FP cavity controls the buildup of vibrational excitation, while simultaneous driving of both optical modes enables stepwise vibrational depletion. These results establish hybrid molecular optomechanical systems as a tunable platform for history-dependent and pulse-driven molecular dynamics, with potential applications in nanoscale memory, multilevel information processing, and optically controlled molecular switching.

title: Entropy production from crossing a quantum separatrix
authors: Peter Stabel, James R. Anglin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26737v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: If the Hamiltonian of a large quantum system depends on a variable parameter, its parameter-dependent energy spectrum may often form a dense lattice of avoided crossings. If the parameter slowly changes, the system's time evolution through the avoided crossings tends in the semi-classical limit to change from adiabatic to diabatic across a narrow energy range that has recently been defined as a quantum separatrix. Here we show that in the extreme semi-classical limit of a quasi-continuously dense spectrum, all quantum separatrices form a universal one-parameter family, and that evolution through the separatrix becomes efficiently ergodizing. If the unitary evolution is realistically averaged over small variations in the parameter time dependence, quantum separatrix crossing generates diagonal entropy according to a universal formula. Numerical examples confirm that the results for quasi-continuous spectra remain clearly recognizable in finite systems, with only small finite-size effects.

title: Efficient Tensor Decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like Potentials and Its Application to Probing Molecular Geometries Using a Quantum Computer
authors: James Brown, Masashi Takahashi, Robert Wodraszka, James Whitfield
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26740v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present an efficient canonical polyadic decomposition of the Coulomb and Coulomb-like potentials in real-space grid representations suited to quantum computing applications. By decomposing the matrix elements of Coulomb-like potentials into low-rank Cartesian components, we achieve $O(N^{1/3})$ T-gate scaling per Coulomb term, where $N$ is the number of grid points (basis functions) per electron, while maintaining high accuracy. This opens a path to significantly reducing the number of basis functions (i.e., qubits) required compared to previous methods by utilizing improved representations of the Coulomb potential that converge faster with grid spacing. The decomposition is also valid for certain pseudopotentials, which can decrease the cost significantly compared to previous work. This efficient decomposition enables the application of block-encoding techniques at larger grid spacings than with previous decompositions, and can therefore be used for algorithms that do not require high energy accuracy. We apply this decomposed Coulomb potential to hydrogen atom energy levels, the helium ground-state energy, and the Hartree-Fock potential energy curve of LiH, and show that modest basis sizes achieve semi-quantitative to quantitative accuracy. As an example of where these faster-converging Coulomb representations can be used on a quantum computer, we discuss their application to probing low-energy molecular geometries, and we estimate the resulting reduction in the cost of real-time evolution.

title: Fully Automated Discovery of Phase Diagrams Using Agentic Large Language Models
authors: Robert Amelung, Maximilian N\"agele, Florian Marquardt
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26749v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Classifying phases of matter and mapping out phase diagrams are central problems in physics. Recently, machine learning techniques have emerged as promising tools for phase classification, ranging from supervised learning to various unsupervised methods. However, these techniques provide limited qualitative insight into the discovered phases, typically work only for specific system classes, and do not by themselves efficiently map out the phase diagram. Autonomously constructing the phase diagram of a general system purely from measurements, without prior knowledge of the system, while also yielding qualitative understanding of the phases, remains an open task. In this work, we introduce Phasonaut, a two-agent framework that leverages the tool-use capabilities and broad knowledge of large language models (LLMs) to drive an active learning loop that constructs phase diagrams of physical systems and provides interpretations of the discovered phases. Starting from scratch, it iteratively selects and performs measurements, analyzes the resulting data, and segments the parameter domain into the phases it discovers. Phasonaut recovers the phase diagrams of classical and quantum spin systems to substantial precision. In the future, this framework could enable rapid exploration of systems with unknown phase diagrams, including in autonomously driven experiments.

title: Geometric properties of Wilsonian flows of periodic potentials in two dimensions
authors: Daniel G. Barci, Nathan O. Silvano
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26753v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Periodic interactions can possess multiple competing minima and barriers, whose evolution under coarse-graining offers a geometric perspective complementary to the scaling of Fourier harmonics. We study this evolution in two dimensions by deriving a functional Wilsonian renormalization-group flow for a general smooth periodic potential and its running sine-Gordon frequency within a constant-kinetic projection. Reaction--diffusion and Burgers representations reveal two key properties of the flow: discrete translation symmetries are preserved, and the number of extrema can only remain constant or decrease. Consequently, the nonlinear generation of Fourier harmonics may accompany a progressive simplification of the potential landscape. We illustrate the role of symmetry with two complementary examples. A weak breaking of the $\pi$-translation symmetry allows a reduction from four extrema to two, whereas a non-sinusoidal interaction retaining this symmetry evolves from eight extrema to the four protected by its periodicity. These results highlight how symmetry and coarse-graining jointly reorganize competing minima and barriers in periodic interactions.

title: Gravity-induced entanglement assisted by an additional interaction using magic angle calibration
authors: Daisuke Miki, Alfred Li, Yanbei Chen
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26755v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Gravity-induced entanglement provides an operational test of whether gravitational dynamics are compatible with local operations and classical communication (LOCC), but the weakness of the gravitational interaction and the presence of force noise make direct entanglement generation extremely demanding. We introduce a controllable additional coherent interaction that biases two test masses close to, but within, a separability-preservation bound, so that the weak Newtonian coupling supplies only the remaining coherent contribution needed for entanglement. If the additional interaction alone is shown to be incapable of generating entanglement, while entanglement is observed when gravity is included, the gravitational interaction provides a non-LOCC contribution. Since gravity cannot be turned off, we use a magic-angle null of the projected tidal coupling to calibrate the additional interaction and force noise. If the additional dynamics is certified to preserve separability at the magic angle and entanglement is subsequently observed in a non-null configuration, the gravitational contribution is incompatible with an LOCC description within the Markovian model. The protocol trades the stringent absolute force-noise requirement of direct schemes for precision in controlling the additional coupling, its backaction, and angle-dependent systematics.

title: Harnessing Dephasing for Quantum Reservoir Computing with a Minimum Complexity Architecture: Applications to Nonlinear Time-Series Prediction
authors: Yicheng Song, Zhipeng Yang, Heng Fan, Gouhei Tanaka
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26762v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum reservoir computing (QRC) exploits quantum dynamics for temporal information processing. Quantum noise affects the reservoir dynamics and can either impair computational performance or serve as a computational resource. However, the role of pure dephasing in Hamiltonian encoding QRC remains unclear. In this work, we propose a minimum complexity QRC model that harnesses pure dephasing in an open uniform XX chain. We show that, under suitable input encoding, pure dephasing can ensure the echo state and fading memory properties even without amplitude damping. Furthermore, in the presence of amplitude damping, the proposed quantum reservoir has distinct stationary states for distinct inputs, and introducing pure dephasing alters these states, thereby affecting the reservoir dynamics. Information processing capacity analysis shows that joint control of the two decoherence mechanisms regulates memory and nonlinearity, providing access to diverse capacity profiles. The proposed QRC achieves promising performance on synthetic benchmarks, while its 6-qubit configuration outperforms all three multi-reservoir echo state network baselines on over half of the real-world prediction tasks. These findings highlight pure dephasing as a computational resource for QRC.

title: Parity-violating optical rotation in the Th-229 nuclear clock transition
authors: Sebastian Lahs, Thorsten Schumm, Victor V. Flambaum, David DeMille
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26784v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition in $^{229}$Th provides a new opportunity to study hadronic parity violation (PV) by optical methods. The PV nucleon--nucleus interaction admixes opposite-parity nuclear states into the $5/2^+$ ground state and the $3/2^+$ isomer, thereby inducing an electric-dipole amplitude $E1_{\rm PV}$ that interferes with the magnetic-dipole clock transition amplitude $M1$. In a single-valence-neutron Nilsson model, we find $|E1_{\rm PV}/M1| \sim 2\times10^{-5}$. This interference can be detected as a parity-violating nuclear optical rotation (PVNOR) of resonant laser light transmitted through a $^{229}$Th-doped crystal. For a highly-doped CaF$_2$ crystal fiber, the estimated rotation is of order $10^{-6}\,{\rm rad}$. A crossed-polarizer measurement can reach this sensitivity with existing ultraviolet laser technology. We also analyze systematic effects in the form of optical birefringence, stray magnetic-field-induced Faraday rotation, and local crystal defects. Such a measurement would provide the first direct probe of the PV neutron-nucleus interaction constant, $g_n$.

title: Benchmark Ne-like Transitions of W, Re, Os, Ir, and Bi Measured by High-resolution TES x-ray Spectroscopy with Absolute Energy Calibration
authors: G. Mondeel (Clemson University, Massachusetts Institute of Technology), C. A. Faiyaz (Clemson University),  Dipti (Clemson University, National Institute of Standards and Technology Gaithersburg), H. Staiger (Clemson University, National Institute of Standards and Technology Gaithersburg), L. Brent (Loyola University Maryland, National Institute of Standards and Technology Gaithersburg), A. C. Gall (Auburn University, Center for Astrophysics | Harvard & Smithsonian), C. I. Szabo (National Institute of Standards and Technology Gaithersburg), G. O'Neil (National Institute of Standards and Technology Boulder), D. S. Swetz (National Institute of Standards and Technology Boulder), P. Szypryt (National Institute of Standards and Technology Boulder, University of Colorado Boulder), J. W. Dean (National Institute of Standards and Technology Boulder, University of Colorado Boulder), Yu. Ralchenko (NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, University of Maryland College Park), E. Takacs (Clemson University, National Institute of Standards and Technology Gaithersburg)
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26801v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present high-resolution measurements of $n=2$-3 transitions in Ne-like tungsten, rhenium, osmium, iridium, and bismuth using a transition-edge sensor (TES) microcalorimeter. These measurements provide new benchmarks for Ne-like ions in the high-$Z$ regime ($Z > 74$), extending previous EBIT studies of the sequence. To achieve sub-eV accuracy, we developed a dedicated x-ray fluorescence source employing well-characterized K-shell emission lines from metallic elements. Our results offer stringent tests for relativistic atomic structure theories and demonstrate the advantage of TES spectroscopy for precision measurements in highly charged ions.

title: Simple Routes to Turing-Like Patterns
authors: Zhan Zhao, Xiang-Ning Li, Wen-Wen Li, Ji-Chong Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26814v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spots, stripes, and networks recur in systems with very different microscopic dynamics, suggesting that the competing processes behind Turing-like patterns may be easy to realise. We ask whether local amplification coupled to suppression over a wider region can generate these geometries in simple systems beyond chemical reaction--diffusion models. We test this idea in two settings, a binary cellular automaton obtained by adding a distant neighbour count to Conway's Game of Life and a self-gravitating toy universe described by particle motion and two continuous fields. The automaton produces spots, stripes, and coexistence across its control plane, while a rule retaining only the two opposing counts produces islands, stripes, and holes. Directional correlations and intrinsic dimension identify the same region of orientational order. In the gravitational system, convergence increases local density while mass transport depletes the surroundings. The two-field and particle densities have a smoothed spatial correlation of $0.962$ at scale factor $a=1$ under the original force law, and strengthening its long-wavelength component drives both descriptions toward fewer dense condensations. Together, these results show how simple counting rules and redistribution of a conserved quantity can realise competing growth and suppression, providing two concrete routes by which Turing-like geometries can recur across different dynamics.

title: Frequency-bin-encoded quantum secret sharing with fast basis switching
authors: Chen-You Su, Suparna Seshadri, Hsuan-Hao Lu, Jason D. McKinney, Andrew M. Weiner, Joseph M. Lukens
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26816v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Frequency-bin encoding offers unique opportunities for fiber-native quantum information processing, yet its full potential has been hampered by challenges in rapid state control and protocol scaling. Leveraging high-speed microwave processing, we overcome several extant hurdles and unlock new fundamental capabilities in frequency-based quantum communications. First, we demonstrate three-party quantum secret sharing, representing, to our knowledge, the first multiparty ($N\geq 3$ users) quantum communication protocol implemented entirely with frequency encoding. Second, we demonstrate active, pseudorandom switching of frequency-bin quantum states and measurement bases at 20 MHz symbol rates, enabling real-time protocol operation without relying on hardware-intensive passive basis-selection schemes. Even under fast switching, we preserve high-contrast three-party correlations ($\geq 0.91$) and low quantum bit error rates ($\leq 4.5\%$). Our work extends frequency-bin quantum communication beyond static, two-party protocols, opening a pathway toward scalable, reconfigurable, and real-time spectrally encoded quantum networking.

title: Feshbach Projection Formalism for Resonant Electrodynamics
authors: Nikolai A. Vlasov, Ekaterina E. Maslova, Andrey Novitsky, Mikhail V. Rybin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26821v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Open resonant photonic systems are widely described by effective non-Hermitian formalisms, such as temporal coupled-mode theory, which capture radiative decay through complex eigenfrequencies. In conventional formulations, however, these effective models remain largely phenomenological, lacking a direct microscopic connection to the underlying Maxwell equations. To bridge this gap, we present an analytically tractable light-matter framework based on the Feshbach projection formalism applied to classical electrodynamics. Starting from a coupled system of mechanical oscillator and a one-dimensional electromagnetic field, we construct a strictly Hermitian first-order Hamiltonian. We demonstrate that rigorously eliminating the electromagnetic degrees of freedom via the outgoing Green's function automatically generates a non-Hermitian mechanical operator. Crucially, the resulting radiative damping is determined by the local electromagnetic response rather than introduced ad hoc. Furthermore, we extend this framework to two spatially separated dipoles and show how field retardation transforms a finite set of discrete modes into a countably infinite Fabry-Perot-like spectrum as the separation deviates from zero. The proposed framework provides an intuitive yet rigorous foundation for deriving effective non-Hermitian dynamics directly from conservative light-matter interactions.

title: Multiconfigurational and Spin-Orbit Extensions of the BSR-RMT Interface
authors: Aaron T. Bondy, Juan C. del Valle, Kathryn R. Hamilton, Klaus Bartschat
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26834v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We report the extension of the B-spline R-matrix (BSR) to R-matrix with time dependence (RMT) interface to include support for multiconfiguration target states and $jK$ coupling, including the one-body spin-orbit (SO) interaction. Inner-region input data generated by BSR are transformed through the interface for time propagation in RMT. Two examples demonstrate the working interface: high-order harmonic generation in helium and weak-field, near-resonance response in carbon. The helium comparisons employ previously studied laser parameters, displaying excellent agreement with the established Belfast R-matrix input codes in the time-dependent dipole and harmonic spectrum, both with and without SO. Further structure comparisons in helium show close agreement in the SO-induced changes in energy and oscillator strengths. The two codes coincide on the much larger SO-induced change in the dipole response in carbon, demonstrating agreement for multiconfigurational target states. These extensions allow the flexibility of BSR structure calculations to be used in time-dependent studies of heavier and more complex atoms.

title: SOP Sensing in Hollow-Core Fiber: Forward Sensing using COTS Transponder and Localization with Coherent OTDR
authors: Adrish Sahu, Rajiv Boddeda, Arnaud Dupas, Carina Castineiras Carrero, Ha\"ik Mardoyan, Sterenn Guerrier, Matteo Lonardi, Javier Errea Moreno, Peng Li, Shuhai Li, Lei Zhang, Jie Luo, Daniel Peterson, J\'er\'emie Renaudier
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26839v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We experimentally investigate and compare distributed state-of-polarization sensing in support-tube hollow-core and standard single-mode fiber. Despite significantly weaker Rayleigh backscattering and reduced polarization sensitivity in hollow-core fiber, polarization perturbations remain observable and spatially localizable, demonstrating the feasibility of SOP-based distributed sensing in hollow-core fiber

title: Coherence Lengths of Laser Pointers
authors: Vaishnavi Rao Namakkal Ranga Rao, Marissa R. Godoy, Mark D. Sotnikov, Justin L. Oliver, Ayane Gomi, Bo Eickelberg, Mariana Rojas-Montoya, Henry B. Wahhab, Christopher L. Smallwood
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26878v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We report on the coherence lengths of low-cost green laser pointers in the midst of multimodal behavior using an optical interferometer based on noncollinear beam geometries and a CMOS detector array. Examined devices include three diode lasers and a frequency-doubled neodymium-emission diode-pumped solid state (DPSS) laser. Coherence length measurements are variable among devices, but values can nevertheless regularly exceed 10 cm. The work serves as a template for an advanced undergraduate physics laboratory experiment and may inspire new kinds of laser pointer devices utilizing interference effects as operative principles.

title: Scheduling the quantum implementation of the Trotter decomposition for Hamiltonian simulation
authors: Augustin Ho (Graduate School of Science and Technology, Keio University, \'Ecole des Mines de Saint-\'Etienne), Naoki Yamamoto (Graduate School of Science and Technology, Keio University, Quantum Computing Center, Keio University)
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26884v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: For the quantum computational task for Hamiltonian simulation, the arrangement in which sub-Hamiltonians appear in the Trotter decomposition may have a large influence on the precision, under a given circuit complexity. In this paper, we design several scheduling strategies by combining two methods; that is, the existing simultaneous diagonalization scheme leveraged in order to guarantee the performance in a relatively short circuit depth, with a method inspired from a Trotter-Suzuki decomposition of the second or the fourth order for a better accuracy. By conducting numerical simulations on various Hamiltonian instances, we confirm a systematic advantage over previous methods. Thus, our proposal may eliminate the need of dealing with several Hamiltonian-dependent scheduling strategies.

title: Dissipative erasure of pulse-to-pulse dispersion imbalance in ultrafast burst-mode lasers
authors: Mesut La\c{c}in, Paul Repgen, Umut Aydemir, Fatih \"Omer Ilday
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26887v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ultrafast GHz bursts enable laser-matter interactions where successive excitations collectively build sustained nonequilibrium states and efficient material interactions. However, directly generating pulse trains at GHz rates remains challenging. Alternatively, repetition-rate multipliers (RRMs) divide each oscillator pulse into equidistant replicas, but either suffer from dispersion imbalances that prevent simultaneous compression or are limited to few pulses per burst. Here, we introduce dissipative erasure, which first suppresses the differences by spectral filtering and then regenerates the optical bandwidth via nonlinear amplification without restoring the erased differences. We derive two scaling results: as the repetition rate increases geometrically with RRM stages, maximum path differences approach a finite limit; meanwhile, dispersive differences weaken quadratically with filtering. We demonstrate dissipative erasure experimentally, generating 100-$\mu$J bursts, comprising thousands of 100-fs pulses at 51.3 GHz, from a Yb-fiber amplifier. Dissipative erasure has diverse potential applications for suppressing deterministic or stochastic differences before recovering desired optical properties.

title: Analog Explorations of Quantum State Measurement
authors: Benjamin Krawciw, James P. Crutchfield
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26889v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The awkward disconnect in the postulates of quantum mechanics between the continuous, deterministic, linear, and unitary evolution governed by Schr\"odinger's equation and the discontinuous, stochastic, nonlinear, and nonunitary measurement process has vexed physicists for decades. Intuition from classical mechanics, statistical mechanics, and dynamical systems theory suggests that such a process might be modeled with a nonlinear system of differential equations. We explore such approaches by designing a deterministic model of an ideal projective measurement on a single qubit and constructing an analog computer that simulates it by manipulating voltages in an electrical circuit. The model reduces to Schr\"odinger evolution when no measurement is taking place. During a measurement, a hidden variable that the observer does not resolve selects the outcome, and the model is constructed so that a uniformly distributed hidden variable yields Born-rule frequencies. We do not derive the Born rule; rather, we show that a deterministic dynamical system with no intrinsic noise can implement it. Over 300 trials, the circuit reproduces the ideal model's individual outcomes to within one percent of the decision threshold, and its outcome frequencies match the Born rule to within about 0.02 in probability. These results are a small but provocative step towards modeling quantum measurement with macro-scale machines---a step of interest for both the foundations of physics and the alternatives to digital computing it suggests.

title: Benchmarking Quantum Key Distribution Hardware Across Operating Conditions
authors: Jerry Horgan, Indrakshi Dey, Hajar Bennouri, Daniel C. Kilper
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26925v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is entering national fibre networks, but published secret key rates (SKRs) are measured over different distances, wavelengths, classical traffic loads and clock rates, so systems are hard to compare. We write the SKR as the product of the transmitter clock rate, the channel transmittance and the secret key per received pulse. This third factor, the noise-normalised key rate (NNKR), needs four commonly reported parameters and depends mainly on the equipment wherever the SKR is proportional to transmittance. A companion metric, the implementation efficiency (IE), compares the SKR with the ideal key rate of its channel, including classical-traffic noise. For fixed loss-limited equipment, NNKR is independent of channel loss, whereas the fraction of the repeaterless bound varies 1.6-fold over 2-25 dB. An analytic model relates the flat loss range of NNKR to the detector noise count rate and dead time. We apply both metrics to ten published coexistence experiments, and NNKR to 42,115 measurements from four systems of two vendors and four high-rate laboratory systems. For one production system, NNKR has a 6.9% coefficient of variation over 17 dB of attenuation and agrees within 0.7 dB with three of four published deployments of that platform. Under coexistence, that platform's NNKR and IE stay within 0.5 dB of their standalone values. In decibels, NNKR is a sum of component penalties, as in an optical link budget, and for one laboratory system the budget from its published parameters and measured secure fraction closes within 0.3 dB.

title: Resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in one-dimensional quantum scattering
authors: V\'ictor M. Villalba
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26960v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We study resonance-controlled post-selected mode entanglement in a one-dimensional quantum-scattering model. Two incoming electrons scatter independently from a symmetric double-barrier structure and the sector with one reflected and one transmitted electron is selected. The idealised delta-function barriers used in earlier work are replaced by exponentially localised cusp barriers, $U(x)=U_0\exp(-|x\mp d/2|/a)$, for which the single-barrier scattering problem is exactly solvable in terms of modified Bessel functions of imaginary order. We derive the corresponding reflection and transmission amplitudes, verify their current normalisation and validate them independently by direct numerical integration. Two separated cusp barriers are then combined through a Fabry-P\'erot composition, whose accuracy is quantified by solving the full two-centre Schr\"odinger equation. In the well-separated regime the approximation reproduces the full resonance positions to high accuracy. The concurrence zeros are controlled by the resonance phase condition $\delta(\kappa)+\kappa d=n\pi$, with a continuously unwrapped single-barrier reflection phase $\delta$. We also calculate the post-selection probability $P_{RT}$, showing explicitly that large conditional concurrence can occur in a low-probability sector. Systematic scans in barrier width, integrated strength and reference momentum show that finite width can shift off-resonant concurrence maxima and, depending on the reference momentum, reduce their attainable height. The results identify resonance-controlled conditional entanglement as a robust feature of the well-separated double-barrier geometry rather than an artefact of the zero-range idealisation.

title: On a Supersymmetric Generalization of the Matytsin Formula
authors: Evgeny Porubov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.26997v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive the leading asymptotics of the supersymmetric analogue of the Itzykson-Zuber integral for the supergroup $U(n|m)$ in the limit $n,m\to\infty$ when $n/m$ is kept finite. This generalizes the Matytsin result for $U(N)$. We show that it is described by the classical action of two independent Hamiltonian systems corresponding to the bosonic and fermionic sectors.

title: Physics-Guided Recursive Self-Improvement of Amortized Bayesian Inference Across Physics
authors: Bo Liang, Mingtao Chen, Minghui Du, Ziren Luo, Guohua Wang, Peng Xu, Zhichao Hu, Maxm Pan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27006v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Across physics, from the orbits of imaged exoplanets and the matter inside neutron stars to thin films at synchrotrons and cortical neurons, conservation laws, interference, and compensating currents compress the posteriors of precise data into tiny, curved regions where Markov chains need minutes to days. We introduce PhyRSI (physics-guided recursive self-improvement), in which an AI agent coupled to the simulator writes and revises an amortized Bayesian inference algorithm for each field, scored by the importance weights of the exact likelihood because the true posterior is unknown. It evolves coordinates, symmetries, and factorizations matched to the physics: orbital elements at the best-measured epoch, Fresnel-normalized reflectivity with a chart for each of its multiple solutions, coordinates along which Na+ and K+ currents compensate, a shared neutron-star equation of state that factorizes a 32-dimensional joint analysis, and the time-rescaling symmetry of predator-prey dynamics. In six fields, networks trained once on simulations return 36 posteriors of real observations in seconds, reweighted by the likelihood and agreeing with converged Markov chains about as closely as two independent chains agree with each other. Such posteriors could steer synchrotron film growth and patch-clamp recordings as they run, follow X-ray transients while they are bright, update the dense-matter equation of state as neutron stars are added, and compare physical models across catalogs. Inference can thus be evolved and checked by the physics itself rather than designed by hand for each problem.

title: Augmenting Quantum Neural Networks with Contractive Layers
authors: Bolin Huang, Pengfei Zhang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27019v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Classical neural networks combine diverse layers with complementary roles to achieve rich expressive capabilities across complex learning tasks. Rapid advances in quantum science and technology have motivated growing interest in their quantum counterparts, quantum neural networks, raising the question of how their expressivity can be enhanced through the design of new quantum layers. Of particular interest are layers that enrich the accessible function space while introducing only a small number of additional trainable parameters. In this Letter, we introduce the contractive layer as a promising building block for quantum neural networks. This layer comprises all-to-all couplings governed by a single trainable parameter, enabling efficient control of quantum information flow while maintaining experimental relevance to Rydberg atom arrays. Using observable learning as a benchmark, we show that contractive layers enhance expressivity more efficiently than simply increasing the depth of conventional brick-wall circuits. This advantage stems from a systematic increase in the accessible target-space dimension per trainable parameter. We further demonstrate similar improvements in image recognition tasks. These results highlight contractive layers as a practical route to expressive quantum neural networks on near-term quantum devices.

title: Generalized Wigner-Yanase Uncertainty Bounds for Multiple Quantum Channels
authors: Jianming Zhou, Xiaoli Hu, Naihuan Jing
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27034v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive uncertainty relations for quantum channels based on the generalized Wigner-Yanase skew information. For three channels, we obtain a product lower bound by optimizing over permutations of commutator and anticommutator pairings. For an arbitrary number of channels, we establish a lower bound on the sum of squared uncertainties and construct a hierarchy of bounds using the partial Cauchy-Schwarz inequality. These bounds are invariant under changes of Kraus representation for a fixed operator basis. The first two levels of the hierarchy coincide with the elementary arithmetic-geometric mean bound, while the intermediate levels generally depend on the ordering of the operator basis. Examples involving three and four qubit channels demonstrate the bounds and compare their performance with an earlier pairing inequality under fixed channel representations.

title: Physical Learning for Autonomous Tuning of Spin Qubits in Electrostatically Defined Quantum Dots
authors: Leonardo Gaytan, Bradley Lloyd, Paul Kliewer, Chandler Wilburn, Lincoln D. Carr, Adam McCaughan, Sonia Buckley, Meenakshi Singh
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27140v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Tuning electrostatically defined quantum dots remains a primary bottleneck in the scalability of semiconductor spin qubits. While existing solutions rely on machine learning algorithms, these approaches require global information, introduce latency bottlenecks, and tax the limited cooling power available at cryogenic stages. Here, we demonstrate an FPGA-in-the-loop learning paradigm that bypasses digital computing overhead by utilizing multiplexed gradient descent (MGD) for tuning. Implemented on an FPGA and an emulated quantum dot device, our system autonomously tracks environmental drift, dynamically recovers from discrete charge jumps, and maintains steady-state stabilization in low signal-to-noise ratio regimes, without prior knowledge of the device's cross-capacitance matrix. The system also navigates the charge-stability landscape to stabilize the quantum dot around optimal operating points. These results demonstrate a ``compute-in-place'' platform, with a logic and power footprint suited to future cryo-CMOS integration, that provides autonomous stabilization of quantum dots at desired operating points, creating an auto-tuning system for spin qubits that is resilient to electrostatic drifts, changing noise profiles, and two-level fluctuations.

title: Adaptive Collective Decision-Making in Signed Networks
authors: Vishnudatta Thota, Aditi Saxena, Twinkle Tripathy, Vaibhav Srivastava
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27147v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Collective decision-making often unfolds in networks where cooperation and antagonism coexist. Such signed interactions arise in social, biological, and robotic systems, and can lead to qualitatively different collective outcomes: consensus, polarization, or clustering. Existing signed network models typically explain these outcomes separately, leaving open how they can emerge within a single dynamical framework. Here, we introduce a generalized Laplacian flow for bi-partitioned signed networks, a class of networks that allows cooperative and antagonistic interactions both within and across two prescribed groups. The proposed model includes an adaptive social effort state, interpreted as a leaky memory of persistent signed network disagreement, which enables bounded and nontrivial steady-states beyond classical signed Laplacian flows. We derive conditions that determine whether the network reaches consensus, polarization, or clustering based on the spectral structure of the generalized Laplacian and effective resistance matrices. The framework applies beyond structurally balanced, weakly balanced, and quasi-structurally balanced networks, and reveals how changes in signed interaction strengths can shift a network between collective decision regimes. We validate the theory on stochastic block model networks, a judicial voting network, and a U.S. senate bill co-sponsorship network. Altogether, our results provide a structural and dynamical account of how mixed cooperative and antagonistic relationships shape emergent collective behaviors.

title: Unconventional Photon Blockade in Second-Order Nonlinearity Coupled Cavities with Asymmetric Dissipation
authors: Zhi-Qiang Zhang, Xiao-Ai Zhang, Yan-Zhe Song, Meng-Li Guo, Yan-Hui Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27200v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate the unconventional photon blockade in a second-order nonlinearity coupled double-cavity system with asymmetric dissipation. By treating the cavity decay rates as independent parameters, we analytically derive two exact families of optimal blockade conditions. While the first family recovers and generalizes the symmetric-dissipation results of previous studies, the second family, arising uniquely from an asymmetric dissipation ratio of $\kappa_B = 2\kappa_A$, completely locks the relative phase of the interference pathways. Importantly, we find that this asymmetric dissipation not only renders the optimal blockade condition strictly immune to frequency detuning, but also enhances the blockade depth by an order of magnitude compared to the resonant case. Furthermore, the mean photon number remains almost unaffected, proving that this enhanced robustness is achieved without sacrificing the brightness of the single-photon source. These findings offer a promising route toward robust single-photon generation in passive cavities with second-order nonlinearity.

title: Probabilistic image generation conditioned on an optical latent code
authors: Yu Shao, Haiqi Gao, Fuyan Wu, Ziyan Zhang, Junren Wen, Yuchuan Shao, Weidong Shen, Chenying Yang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27230v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: While diffractive optical networks compress images into compact representations, such measurements have predominantly served discriminative inference or deterministic reconstruction. Here we demonstrate probabilistic image generation conditioned solely on a 16_bit binary optical latent code (OLC) formed by a diffractive encoder and binarized camera readout. The intentionally many-to-one mapping makes each OLC specify a class of OLC-compatible images rather than a unique reconstruction target. An OLC_conditioned conditional variational autoencoder (CVAE) learns this distribution, while optical re-encoding promotes consistency between generated images and the measured OLC. Numerical characterization and proof-of-concept acquisition with a spatial light modulator_camera system establish the OLC as a physically accessible generative condition. On MNIST, samples generated from a single OLC vary in morphology while preserving class identity, and their optical-recognition accuracy reaches 81.6%, close to the 81.9% obtained from the source OLCs. These results link compact optical sensing to probabilistic synthesis of optically recognizable images.

title: Efficient convolution-based nonparaxial propagation of partially coherent light
authors: Rafael de la Fuente Herrezuelo
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27232v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We derive an efficient formulation for wide-angle propagation of partially coherent light from extended incoherent sources, extending the generalized van Cittert-Zernike Schell (GVS) propagator beyond the paraxial regime with absolute radiometric normalization. Within the Fresnel model, we establish that GVS and the classical paraxial source-PSF convolution are algebraically equivalent, explicitly deriving the corresponding source inversion, magnification, and absolute radiometric normalization. The resulting separation of mapped source and coherent pupil response enables wide-angle convolution in direction-cosine coordinates. Within a physically motivated diffracted-radiance formulation, this far-field convolution is exact for incoherent plane-wave mixtures. The same power prescription also relates delta-correlated source statistics to Lambertian radiance and hemispherical emitted power. At finite distances, we use a common incident curvature and approximate the source contributions by shifting and weighting a single coherent monitor response in direction-cosine coordinates. The differentiable formulation supports gradient-based inverse design of diffractive elements and metasurfaces represented by scalar pupils. Examples reveal geometric distortion and irradiance fall-off missed by the paraxial models and demonstrate wide-angle beam shaping at finite distances. A benchmark shows orders of magnitude faster evaluation than source-by-source propagation with a common error tolerance.

title: Stinespring's Dilation, Universal-NOT, and Limitations of Quantum Uncoupled Learning
authors: Emmanouil-Vasileios Vlatakis-Gkaragkounis, Pucheng Xiong
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27251v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Uncoupled learning, in which players know only their own payoff, are a standard model of decentralized learning toward Nash equilibrium. We study their quantum counterpart, where strategies are quantum states and, in each round, a player receives a physical copy of their opponent's current strategy and updates their own state by a quantum channel. This adds to uncoupledness a constraint with no classical analogue: every update must be physically realizable. In fact, this constraint is decisive in conjugation games, in which Bob has a strictly dominant pure strategy and Alice's unique best response is its transpose. In this work, we show some limitations of uncoupled (learning) dynamics in finding the Nash equilibrium for conjugation games. First, we prove that no autonomous, memoryless, uncoupled dynamics converge to Nash equilibrium in a family of four single-qubit conjugation games. Specifically, any memoryless channel that keeps all four equilibria fixed will leave Alice's strategy frozen. This result also extends to $4^n$ games on $n$-qubit registers. Second, we show that this barrier disappears with a small classical memory: for any finite family of $L$ pure targets, a guess-and-test rule with $O(\log L)$ classical bits converges to equilibrium, with an explicit bound on its convergence rate. Finally, we prove that no finite memory, classical or quantum, suffices for the continuum of all pure-qubit targets. Our proof of the impossibility for memoryless channels relies on Stinespring's dilation theorem, while the impossibility for finite-memory channels relies on the optimal universal-NOT (in)fidelity bound by Bu\v{z}ek, Hillery, and Werner.

title: Pulse-tube-vibration induced Larmor frequency jitter in anisotropic Kramers spins
authors: R. Shaik, P. Kesarwani, S. Rajendran, S. E. Kubatkin, A. V. Danilov, S. E. de Graaf, V. Ranjan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27267v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We investigate the role of pulse-tube mechanical vibrations towards spin frequency noise in a cryogen-free dilution refrigerator. Our system comprises of a low mode-volume superconducting resonator coupled to 50 ppm $\text{Er}^{3+}:\text{CaWO}_4$ spins with highly anisotropic g-factors. By measuring single-shot spin echoes using narrow-bandwidth three-pulse sequences, we directly observe a vibration induced stochastic signal resulting from the spin's Larmor frequency moving into and out of the detection bandwidth. The sensitivity to these vibrations is substantially suppressed when a) the external magnetic field is aligned along the symmetry c-axis and b) spin temperature is modestly increased to 60~mK. We also benchmark the system as a quantum sensor for angular fluctuations, extracting a noise floor of 350 nanodegrees.

title: Consecutive Supersymmetric Quantum Mechanical Algorithms for Resolving the Spectra of Legendre-type Differential Operators
authors: Tianchun Zhou
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27295v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quite comprehensive iterative algorithms based on consecutive supersymmetric quantum mechanics (SUSYQM) have been constructed heuristically, for resolving the eigenspectra of the Legendre operator and its associates parametrized in various coordinates, \emph{without receiving any input from traditional analytical methods}. On building these algorithms, the two symmetries \text{--} supersymmetry and shape invariance symmetry \text{--} hidden in these operators are brought to the fore as the only two governing principles, with the aids of the newly devised algebraic techniques such as the \emph{active supersymmetrization transformations}, \emph{momentum operator maps} as well as plain and \emph{higher-order spin matrix maps}. In view of their algebraic simplicity and elegance, high efficiency, as well as independence of traditional methods, some of these algorithms become the promising candidates to supplant the popular power series approach to the eigenspectra of Legendre-type operators.

title: Symplectic Matroids, Stabilizer Codes, and Quantum Secret-Sharing
authors: Sayantan Ganguly
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27300v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: An $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear $[[n,k]]_q$ stabilizer code is represented by a totally isotropic subspace of $\mathbb{F}_q^{2n}$ of dimension $n-k$, whose full-rank generator matrix has nonzero maximal minors on admissible column sets forming the bases of a representable symplectic matroid. Sarvepalli asked whether graphical symplectic matroids introduced by Chow give stabilizer codes with good parameters, when a Lagrangian matroid induces a quantum access structure, which code realizes it, and which polynomial carries the weight enumerator. We answer these questions. For a $3$-connected simple graph, every representation of a graphical symplectic matroid, over any field, gives a stabilizer code of distance exactly $2$, so the girth is not a lower bound. For a represented Lagrangian matroid and a dealer, we construct the dealer-shortened stabilizer code, its logical operators, an encoding isometry and explicit recovery maps, and we show that this is the code implemented by the stabilizer state through teleportation. A set of players recovers the secret, learns nothing, or learns part of it according to a rank formula on pairs of columns, which equals its mutual information with the dealer; for graph states it becomes a cut-rank condition. Over $\F_2$ a symplectic matroid of any rank has only one representation, so the code, its access structure and its weight enumerators depend on the matroid alone; for $q\ge3$ even the enumerator does not. Circuit-induced authorized sets always reconstruct when the matroid is self-dual, but not in general, and a six-qubit graph state shows that the two access structures can differ even then. Finally, a polynomial in the ranks of column pairs determines both weight enumerators.

title: Composite Dielectric-Loaded Metallic Metagratings for Dual-Polarized Transmissive Beam Manipulation
authors: Vitali Specktor, Yuval Singer, Ilya Varenisov, Ariel Epstein
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27311v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We present and experimentally demonstrate a comprehensive analytical suite for the design of transmissive metal-based metagratings (MGs) for dual-polarized anomalous refraction. Considering a composite configuration of perforated metallic slabs with controlled dielectric loading, we develop a rigorous mode-matching formulation tying the various MG degrees of freedom to the various reflected and transmitted Floquet-Bloch modes, enabling efficient beam deflection for both transverse electric (TE) and transverse magnetic (TM) polarizations. Inherently versatile, the analytical framework accurately models single-layer and double-layer constructs with multiple rectangular perforations per unit cell, each potentially loaded with dielectric material. We harness this degree-of-freedom abundance to devise diverse polarization-sensitive transmissive MGs, ranging from all-metallic single-layer and double-layer structures for single-polarized (TM or TE) perfect anomalous refraction, to dielectric-loaded architectures implementing dual-polarized routing of the incident wave. Beyond highlighting concrete paths to address TE-polarized fields in such formations, our results, validated via full-wave simulations and experiments at K band, showcase the great potential of metal-based MGs for manipulating fields in transmission, facilitating effective synthesis of durable dual-polarized beamforming superstrates for environmentally demanding and high power antenna applications.

title: 60-cm-long In-vacuum Zerodur Optical Cavity for Optical Lattice Atom Interferometry
authors: Philip Wondrak, Paola Luna, Kenneth Nakasone, Andrei Zhukov, Michael Grisham, Garrett D. Cole, Po-han Chen, Cristian D. Panda
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27328v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Optical cavities are widely used in atomic physics experiments to control the spatial geometry and spectral properties of atom-light interactions. Recently, an optical lattice generated by the pristine mode of an optical cavity was utilized to hold and extend the quantum coherence of atomic spatial superpositions. Here, we describe an in-vacuum optical cavity designed to enhance the spatial and temporal coherence of optical lattice atom interferometers to one millimeter wavepacket separations and one minute measurement durations. The cavity uses a rigid Zerodur spacer to suppress the negative effects of thermal drift and mechanical-acoustic vibrations on the atomic motional state. The 60 cm-long cavity spacer provides ample optical access for the laser beams and imaging optics necessary for the preparation, quantum control, and read-out of the atomic state, as well as room for various source mass configurations for localized gravitational measurements. An integrated differential pumping structure enables compatibility with ultrahigh-vacuum operation and optical interferometry allows for in-situ vibration monitoring. The performance of the optical cavity is methodically characterized: we measure mirror vibration noise with amplitude below 5 nm/$\sqrt{\rm Hz}$ in a wide frequency range of 2 Hz - 100 kHz and a slow 15 MHz thermal drift of the cavity resonance over 47 hours, which can be readily stabilized with an integrated piezo. The optical cavity supports both 852-nm light for Raman transitions and 1064-nm light for the optical lattice, with a free spectral range matched to an integer divisor of the cesium ground-state hyperfine splitting.

title: Monolithic ultraviolet-to- near infrared photodetection enabled by an aluminium oxide photonic platform
authors: Firehun T. Dullo, Marco Povoli, Ozhan Koybasi, Michael N. Getz, Daniel N. Wright
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27333v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Broadband photonic integrated circuits require waveguide platforms that combine low optical loss across a wide spectral range with integrated photodetection. Here we demonstrate a monolithically integrated atomic-layer-deposited (ALD) aluminium oxide (Al$_2$O$_3$)-on-silicon platform enabling waveguide-coupled photodetection from the ultraviolet to the near-infrared. The architecture employs evanescent coupling between low-loss Al$_2$O$_3$ waveguides and silicon p-i-n photodiodes. The platform supports photodetection at 375, 658 and 780 nm, extending integrated silicon photodetection into the ultraviolet. The devices exhibit linear photocurrent scaling with optical power, dark currents of approximately 2 pA at 50 V reverse bias and nanosecond-scale temporal response. We further demonstrate centimetre-scale ultraviolet Mach-Zehnder interferometer circuits with integrated photodiodes. The same detector architecture is implemented with Si$_3$N$_4$ waveguides, whereas the lower ultraviolet propagation loss of Al$_2$O$_3$ enables an approximately 15-fold higher photodetection response at 375 nm. These results establish ALD Al$_2$O$_3$ as a broadband integrated photonics platform for sensing, spectroscopy and quantum technologies.

title: Trotter Error Bounds in Lean 4 with a Cancellation-Aware Analysis of the Fourth-Order Suzuki Formula
authors: Bingyu Xia, Jue Xu, Yue Wang
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27359v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We formalize the commutator-scaling bound of Childs et al. in Lean 4. For skew-adjoint generators, the local order condition gives an explicit integer step count sufficient to meet a prescribed error tolerance. We apply the theorem in Lean to the binary fourth-order Suzuki formula. For this formula we can also account for cancellation within and between steps. Using local remainder estimates of Casas and Murua, we sum the signed quintic and centered seventh-degree error terms after conjugating each to the interaction picture. For every positive integer step count, we bound the difference between this sum and the global error operator. At fixed time the explicit remainder is eighth order in the step size, and the integral of the conjugated quintic term gives the exact leading error coefficient. The Lean proofs cover the two-generator finite-sum estimates, including the spectral norm for complex matrices.
  On five ten-site nearest-neighbor Heisenberg instances at time $10$ and tolerance $10^{-3}$, the transported sum meets the tolerance at a mean of $129.4$ steps. Taking a separate norm at each step with the same polynomial and remainder gives a mean first crossing between $184.6$ and $185.2$ steps. The accumulated Casas--Murua local bound at $q=8$ gives a mean of $184.8$ steps.

title: Pushy Random Walk on the Bethe lattice: a Galton-Watson perspective
authors: J\'er\'emie Klinger
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27386v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Pushy random walks are minimal models of transport in deformable media, in which the walker displaces the obstacles it bumps into rather than being blocked by them. On the Bethe lattice, we show that the walkable structure dynamically created by a pushy walker can be generated a priori as an explicit multi-type Galton-Watson tree, so that the walker reduces to a simple random walk on a static random tree, and its escape to infinity coincides with the survival of the underlying branching process. Standard generating-function tools then give direct access to the escape properties of these walks. For the Sokoban walk, which pushes a single obstacle, we recover the known critical density $\rho_c = 1-(z-1)^{-2}$ and the behavior of the escape probability close to $\rho_c$, and derive its small-density asymptotics. For the second-order pushy walk, which can push trains of two obstacles, we establish the conjectured $\rho_c = 1-(z-1)^{-3}$, and compute the escape probability at all densities. Beyond escape, the same framework yields the statistics of the trace of trapped walkers: the distribution of the maximal depth follows from the extinction probabilities, while the distributions of the visited volume and of the number of dead ends are encoded in explicit functional equations for their generating functions, which we invert numerically. All predictions agree with Monte Carlo simulations.

title: Hall effect in electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager theory
authors: Yury Budkov, Nikolai Kalikin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27392v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: A self-consistent statistical-mechanical theory of the Hall effect in electrolyte solutions is developed by extending the self-consistent Debye-Huckel-Onsager (SCDHO) framework to crossed electric and magnetic fields. The theory incorporates non-local ionic charge distributions through Slater-type form factors and ion-specific coefficients describing the effective Lorentz response, with experimental input for protons and hydroxide ions. Within the random-phase approximation, the Hall conductivity is expressed as mean-field, correlation, and electrophoretic contributions. Both interaction channels include the Lorentz rotation of the complete electric-field-induced ionic velocity. In the point-charge limit with hydrodynamics suppressed, the relaxation correction agrees with independent odd stochastic density functional theory and the relaxation part of Friedman's classical result. For 22 dilute aqueous electrolytes, the mean absolute relative deviations from measured Hall constants and Hall numbers are about 17 percent. At finite concentrations, the theory predicts a nonmonotonic Hall number for NaBPh4 and sign changes of the electrophoretic correction for NaI and HCl. Correlation effects dominate for HCl and LiOH, whereas the two interaction channels become comparable for KOH and aqueous imidazolium salts. The results clarify how ionic mobilities, effective Hall coefficients, charge distributions, and solvent hydrodynamics determine electrolyte magnetotransport.

title: Quantum computing for gearing down complex many-fermion problems
authors: Weijie Du, Filippo Fornetti, James P. Vary
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27402v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Quantum computing unlocks exciting opportunities to extend first-principles calculations of quantum many-body systems beyond classical computing limits. Despite advances in algorithms and proof-of-principle experiments, large-scale {\it ab initio} calculations on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) devices remain challenging. We introduce a quantum-classical framework that identifies compact single-particle bases to bring otherwise intractable many-fermion problems within classical reach while preserving an accurate ground-state description. We develop an efficient adaptive search scheme driven by simulated annealing that jointly optimizes natural-orbital-guided transformations and active-space selections. A quantum-assisted ground-state estimator provides search guidance using low-depth circuits and relaxed accuracy requirements, making the framework promising for NISQ devices. We demonstrate the framework's applicability for the nuclear structure of the oxygen isotopes. Our framework opens a new route to tackling complex {\it ab initio} many-fermion problems across disciplines through quantum-assisted basis reduction.

title: How many states does an exact relaxation model need? Sharp state complexity and geometric obstructions for reversible chains
authors: Murad Aznagulov
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27406v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: How many states does a reversible Markov model need to reproduce two prescribed relaxation modes exactly? We maximize the smaller of the two stationary coordinate variances over all finite reversible chains whose states lie in a given convex region and whose coordinates relax at rates $1$ and $\rho$. Detailed balance turns this into the equilibrium of a tension-only cable network whose loads depend on the stationary masses.
  For the moment curve of the Wright-Fisher diffusion no finite chain is optimal: maximizing sequences converge to a unique beta law, and the best deficit with $N$ states is of order $N^{-2}$. We find the exact leading constant for states on the curve and for states in its convex hull, together with the optimal cube-root density of states. The hull constant is the curve constant times $c/(1+c)$, $c=(\rho-2)/\rho$; at $\rho=5/2$ the hull needs $\sqrt{6}$ times fewer states, although the limiting law is the same. For $\rho>8/3$ any upward enlargement of the hull lowers the constant again. All lower bounds hold for arbitrary transition graphs.
  At every fixed number of states an optimizer exists. On a seven-gon the smallest optimal chain jumps from three to four states while the optimal value stays constant, and a family of polygons forces the state count to grow linearly with the number of sides. Monotone vector fields give exact upper certificates, which solve an asymmetric quadrilateral at all rates and 381 polygon-rate instances in exact arithmetic. We formulate a finite-realizability problem and a finite-dictionary conjecture for polygons, and derive state budgets and exclusion tests for finite kinetic models.

title: Structure-preserving compression of Matrix Product States
authors: Pouriya Ghadimi, Maximilian Fr\"ohlich, Aaron Sander, Martin Eigel, Richard M. Milbradt
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27408v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Matrix product state time evolution relies on compression to control the growth of bond dimensions, but compression can break the conservation laws of the equation being solved. A truncation is not the flow of a Hermitian generator, so even a small truncation error can violate exact algebraic identities of the Schr\"odinger equation. For any matrix product state integrator that leaves the state in canonical form with an orthogonality center, a scalar correction restores an admissible global invariant after compression whenever the resulting scalar quadratic constraint equation admits a real root, without enlarging any bond dimension. Rank-preserving recovery searches other canonical centers when that correction fails. The geometry of the low-rank manifold provides sufficient conditions for conservation by the fixed-rank projected flow and bounds what corrections within a frozen center frame can achieve. Numerical experiments demonstrate that recovery can be required even along accurate truncated trajectories.

title: Explicit construction of the normal cone at every nonlocal extreme behaviour of $\mathcal{Q}_{2222}$ and device-independent applications
authors: Yutian Wu, Xie Sicheng, Ravishankar Ramanathan
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27413v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The set of quantum correlations $\mathcal{Q}_{2222}$, in the simplest Bell scenario with two parties performing two binary measurements each, is an object of fundamental interest both in quantum foundations and for device-independent applications. A nonlocal extremal quantum behaviour in this set can maximize many different Bell expressions, yet these expressions are not all equally useful in a practical experiment. Here, firstly, we give an explicit characterization of every Bell expression maximized by any given nonlocal extremal quantum behaviour in this Bell scenario. This determines the full normal cone at every such behaviour and makes it possible to optimize over all Bell tests with the same ideal behavior. We then derive an exact variational formula for the quantum bound of an arbitrary Bell expression in this scenario. As an example illustrating the construction, we derive the normal cone for a family of extremal quantum behaviours of importance in device-independent randomness certification, from Phys. Rev. Lett. 129, 150403, 2022. Finally, we explore the consequences of this characterization for device-independent randomness generation in practical experiments. Specifically, for any given detection efficiency $\eta \in [0.75,0.98]$, we construct Bell tests and two-qubit experiments that certify more single-round min-entropy from one Bell score than any CHSH score can certify with the same detector efficiency, even when the quantum devices used for the CHSH test are optimized. The results provide a systematic way to choose Bell tests for a desired quantum behaviour and to improve their performance for device-independent applications under experimental imperfections.

title: Reset Quantum Channels
authors: Thomas Argoud, Alain Joye
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27417v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We introduce Reset Quantum Channels (RQCs), a class of quantum channels acting on a Hilbert space structured as a direct sum of an arbitrary number of subspaces. Within each subspace, the state evolves unitarily; across subspaces, it is transferred by measure-and-prepare resets along given states. In this general setting, we show that the determination of their invariant states reduces to a stochastic eigenvalue problem, whose size is set by the number of reset states rather than by the dimension of the Hilbert space, and we discuss the uniqueness of these states. We further address the primitivity and the spectrum of these channels, which we compute explicitly when the reset states commute with the unitary evolutions. Applications include a small system coupled to several thermal reservoirs. We also consider random unitary evolutions and analyze the averages of the invariant states in this setup. Finally, we show that a suitable continuous-time limit yields Lindblad generators of reset type on the algebra of block-diagonal operators.

title: Ultrafast imaging of ring currents in atoms and condensed matter by electron scattering
authors: Zhongchen Xing, Xinbao Liu, Peixiang Lu, Eberhard K. U. Gross, Zheng Li
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27420v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Ring currents are well known to generate magnetic fields. Despite the rich phenomena and detection of the ring current, an experimental reconstruction of the ring current at the atomic scale is still unsolved. In this work, we propose a method of resolving the ring current in a sample at the atomic scale by ultrafast electron diffraction. Inspired by the Rosenbluth formula, we study the electron diffraction of a sample with a ring current and separate the scattering cross sections into three kinds of response functions, which stand for the electric part, the magnetic part and the cross term, respectively. The ring current in the sample can be reconstructed from measuring the response function in different scattering configurations. Also, following the Rosenbluth formula, we propose that the response functions can be measured by fitting over fixed momentum transfer with different incident energy and relative direction, which is similar to the $\psi$-scan in crystal diffraction. With high-precision ultrafast electron diffraction, the magnetic part will be resolved despite being much weaker than the electric part. We simulate three examples with ring currents -- an ideal hydrogen atom, a circularly polarized helium atom ensemble, and a lithium crystal. Our model offers a promising way to resolve the current structure at the atomic scale.

title: Conductivity of electrolyte solutions: Self-consistent Debye-H\"{u}ckel-Onsager theory
authors: Yury Budkov, Nikolai Kalikin
abstract:
arXiv:2611.27430v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: This study presents a novel approach to addressing the limitations in understanding the behavior of charged particles in solutions. The approach is based on the development of the Self-Consistent Debye-H\"uckel-Onsager (SCDHO) theory, which integrates the effects of non-local charge distributions using a Slater-type charge form factor model. This results in a modified Coulomb potential at short distances, unlike traditional approaches such as the classical Debye-H\"uckel-Onsager theory. The proposed method relies on explicit expressions derived from gradients of local chemical potentials rooted in classical Density Functional Theory (DFT) and the Ornstein-Zernike formalism for correlation functions. Our theoretical framework enables the derivation of analytic equations that describe both correlation (aka relaxation) and electrophoretic contributions to total electric conductivity. Within the established theoretical framework, the model of smeared charges with Slater-type charge form factors provides an accurate predictive tool that can be applied to a wide range of ion valences, concentrations, and temperatures, including both aqueous and non-aqueous electrolyte solutions.
